questions.text: I like to be the one who determines the scope of what the team works on.
I can tell when someone is keeping a conversation going longer than natural because they are avoiding being alone.
I am the person who asks the team how they would like to frame a problem.
I'd rather commit quickly to a direction and learn from the results than test endlessly.
I tend to fill gaps in any group without being asked—whatever is missing, I provide.
My sleep schedule shifts depending on what I'm engaged with; I follow my energy.
I notice when someone is testing the waters with a comment before committing to an opinion.
When suffering is described in vivid detail, it still carries little weight for me.
I tend to evaluate any group activity by asking what I personally stand to gain.
I want to be part of shaping how a project unfolds, alongside others.
I notice that my emotional sensitivity means I am deeply affected by the tone of a room, a text, or a glance.
Seeing someone I don't know in real trouble makes me care about their wellbeing.
I do not naturally sense when a friend group has an inner circle and an outer circle.
When things go sideways, I look for a collective response rather than taking personal charge.
I seldom feel pulled to respond when someone around me is having a hard time.
I routinely optimize my schedule around my own peak performance.
I sense when a group is tacitly agreeing to lower the emotional register of a conversation to keep things safe.
I generally do not analyze why someone chose a particular word when a simpler one would do.
I schedule thinking time into my calendar rather than leaving reflection to chance.
I wake from nightmares with my heart pounding and the fear persisting long after I'm fully awake.
I can work effectively in chaotic environments that would distract most people.
Suffering among people whose lives are very different from mine still matters to me.
I have been told that I have a commanding presence.
I rarely pick up on the implicit rules of a new social group without being told.
I find it hard to ignore a person's pain just to stay comfortable.
I would downsize my own living situation to free up resources for people who need help.
I feel that pursuing mastery in my chosen field is worth more than diversifying my efforts for others.
I break vague goals into concrete next actions so I always know what to do next.
My system seems to auto-regulate emotional intensity without requiring conscious effort.
I tend to feel emotions at a manageable intensity rather than at their extremes.
My emotional life has a consistent, predictable quality that I've come to rely on.
When I get frustrated, the frustration escalates rapidly to a peak.
I protect focused work time by blocking it on my calendar so no one can interrupt it.
I frequently redefine objectives when I think the current ones are wrong.
I am somewhat less moved by other people's hardships than most people I know.
I would turn down a dream job if accepting it meant abandoning someone who depends on me.
